historical_claims.anchor: Sam calls Frodo his master for much of the novel.
He disobeys Frodo's plan to leave alone.
Legolas and Gimli begin with the old distrust between Elves and Dwarves.
Boromir's attempt to take the Ring is a betrayal of the mission.
This is why the ending gives Sam an ordinary house rather than a command over the world's great affairs.

work.note: The existing primary bibliography and claim 027200-c02 date publication of the three volumes 1954–1955; this does not date the fictional history of Middle-earth.

description: Follows the struggle over the Ring, examining power, mercy, fellowship, language, historical depth, war, and the costs of returning home. Covers Sam and the language of service; Friendship across inherited hostility; Boromir and the possibility of repair; The fellowship cannot save everybody.
